evidence: Ov. M. 8.679: totiēns haustum crātēra replērī
terms.comment: Lewis & Short’s first sense is “fill again, refill”. Ovid uses it of the mixing bowl of Baucis and Philemon, which filled itself again as often as it was drained.

terms.gloss: add: pour in more, top up
evidence: Mart. 9.93.1: Addere quid cessās, puer, inmortāle Falernum?
terms.comment: What a drinker calls to the boy who serves the wine; for “another glass”, ask for alterum pōculum.

phrases.english: Just a drop more; that’s enough.

phrases.latin: Addere quid cessās, puer, inmortāle Falernum? quadrantem duplicā dē seniōre cadō.
phrases.english: Why are you slow to pour in more of the immortal Falernian, boy? Double the measure, from an older jar.

phrases.latin: Intereā totiēns haustum crātēra replērī sponte suā per sēque vident succrēscere vīna
phrases.english: Meanwhile they see the mixing bowl, drained so often, fill again of its own accord, and the wine well up by itself

sources: Lewis & Short: repleo · Lewis & Short: addo
